text: {"rules":[{"id":"SKIN-CA-COUNSEL-6MO-24","version":"March 2018","title":"Skin cancer prevention: UV-exposure counseling for persons aged 6 months to 24 years with fair skin types","source_quote":"The USPSTF recommends counseling young adults, adolescents, children, and parents of young children about minimizing exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation for persons aged 6 months to 24 years with fair skin types to reduce their risk of skin cancer.","grade":"B","effective_date":"March 2018","action":"Counsel the patient, or the parent of a young child, about minimizing exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation.","denominator":"{\"all\": [{\"age\": {\"min\": 1, \"max\": 24, \"at\": \"end\"}, \"quote\": \"aged 6 months to 24 years\", \"derived\": {\"min\": \"The text says 6 months, but ages must be whole years. The minimum is set to 1 so infants younger than 6 months are never included; this deliberately leaves out children aged 6-11 months.\"}}, {\"uncomputable\": {\"needs\": \"Fitzpatrick skin type / fair skin assessment (not reliably held in structured EHR data)\"}, \"quote\": \"with fair skin types\"}], \"quote\": \"for persons aged 6 months to 24 years with fair skin types\"}","numerator":"{\"uncomputable\": {\"needs\": \"Documentation that the patient (or the parent of a young child) was counseled about minimizing UV radiation exposure; no counseling interval is stated in the text\"}, \"quote\": \"counseling young adults, adolescents, children, and parents of young children about minimizing exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation\"}","exclusions":"[]"}],"coverage_notes":["The lower age bound of 6 months cannot be expressed in whole years. The rule uses min age 1 (declared as derived), so infants aged 6-11 months are not covered. Human review is needed.","Fair skin type is encoded as uncomputable. Skin type (for example Fitzpatrick type) is not reliably held in structured EHR data, so the denominator cannot be fully computed.","Counseling documentation has no concept in the vocabulary, and the text states no frequency or interval. The numerator is therefore encoded as uncomputable rather than inventing a concept or a lookback window.","For young children, the counseling may go to the parents rather than the patient. This recipient distinction is captured only in the uncomputable numerator's description.","The DATE field carries an asterisk ('March 2018 *') whose footnote is not included in the section text. Its meaning is not represented."]}
